question: Will Lebanon's cabinet refer the Dahr al-Baidar explosives case to the Judicial Council before November 28, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is No: the referral request has been pending since Oct 22 with repeated deferrals, a cabinet 'understanding' to postpone until investigations mature, and Berri/Hezbollah/Amal opposed. Only ~11 days and ~2 likely sessions remain. Upward pressure: the MTV/Naharnet report (Nov 13) that Aoun and Salam agreed to put the file on an upcoming agenda soon, and the ongoing LF boycott cost. Downward pressure: a Nov 15 judicial source (Lebanon24) says a presidential understanding exists to block referral and that a vote would draw only ~5 yes votes; MTV earlier described Aoun/Salam as stalling pending a settlement with Berri. Even if it gets onto an agenda, another deferral is plausible. No human market found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi.
calls.dossier:
- Oct 5, 2026: ISF seized ~780 kg explosives (TNT, C-4, PETN) at Dahr al-Baidar checkpoint; two Hezbollah members arrested (Naharnet, judicial officials).
- Oct 22 session (Baabda): agenda item 7 was the Justice Ministry request to refer the Dahr al-Baidar + al-Qasr explosives to the Judicial Council; after ~4 hours of debate cabinet postponed, saying investigations proceed 'without ceiling' and the request would be considered as the probe progresses (Janoubia, Asharq Al-Awsat, Oct 22-23).
- Oct 26 (tayyar.org): Justice Minister Nassar said he would re-table the referral in ~two weeks; Nassar says Aoun/Salam back the referral in principle but dispute the timing.
- Oct 29-30: LF ministers boycotted the session; MTV (Oct 30) cited sources describing Aoun/Salam as 'stalling' while awaiting a settlement with Speaker Berri; LF threatens escalation.
- Oct 30: military court commissioner Judge Claude Ghanem charged 13 people; file with investigating judge Ghada Abu Alwan (LWJ, LBCI).
- Naharnet: Berri advised Aoun/Salam against referral to avoid confrontation with Hezbollah; Hezbollah/Amal ministers oppose; LF + Kataeb support.
- Nov 13 (MTV via Naharnet): Aoun and Salam 'reached a conclusion' to soon put the referral on an upcoming cabinet agenda. The same day the session (3:30pm) dealt with electricity; LF Energy Minister Saddi attended for the electricity plan only, and the other 3 LF ministers kept boycotting (LBCI, L'Orient Today).
- Nov 15 (Lebanon24): a senior judicial source opposes referral on legal grounds (no evidence of domestic use) and claims a presidential agreement exists to prevent referral; says a vote would yield only ~5 yes votes (Kataeb + 4 LF); recommends not raising it in cabinet.
- Cabinet cadence: usually weekly, Thu/Fri afternoons, announced at short notice; cancellations and postponements are common (the Nov 5 session slipped a week). Searched for the agenda of the next session (~Nov 19-21): not found.
- Status quo: no referral; the request has been pending since Oct 22 through ~3 sessions without a decision.
- Resolves off a reported Council of Ministers decision to refer (in principle counts), not a military-judiciary or Justice Ministry action; a deferral or withdrawal = No.
- Event window: now -> Nov 27, 2026 sessions inclusive (before Nov 28 Beirut time); as of Nov 16, about 2 possible sessions remain.
- Markets: none found on Polymarket/Manifold; Kalshi not applicable.
- Searched but not found: an official agenda listing the item for the next session; any Hezbollah/Amal signal of acquiescence; any vote-count reporting beyond the Lebanon24 source.
calls.reference_class: Contested Lebanese cabinet decisions opposed by the Shiite duo, repeatedly deferred, within a ~2-session window

calls.reasoning: Status quo is No: the Justice Ministry's referral request has been deferred since Oct 22. Two reports describe an Aoun–Berri–Salam understanding not to refer: Al Jadeed (Nov 3) and Lebanon24 (Nov 15). The Shiite duo flatly rejects referral, and cabinet works by consensus, so even if the file reaches an agenda, deferral or a softer formula is the typical Lebanese outcome. Upward pressure: the MTV (Nov 13) report that Aoun and Salam will 'soon' put the item on an agenda, the costly Lebanese Forces boycott, and US pressure. Only about 1–2 sessions remain before Nov 28 (around Nov 20 and Nov 27). Disruption is likely: a public-sector strike and closure this week, and Independence Day on Nov 22. No human prediction market found.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on almost every fact: the Oct 22 deferral, the ongoing Lebanese Forces boycott, the Nov 13 MTV report, the Nov 15 Lebanon24 judicial source, and no market. The factual differences are small. (1) Run 2 reports that the cabinet promised a dedicated session within two weeks of Oct 22 and never held it. Run 1 says the justice minister planned to re-table the request in about two weeks. These are compatible, and the failure to follow through only reinforces the pattern of stalling. (2) Only Run 2 mentions the strike and closure this week, which I cannot verify. If true, it slightly lowers the chance of a session around Nov 20. (3) Only Run 3 cites Al Jadeed (Nov 3) on a 'no referral' understanding. It is consistent with the Lebanon24 report, which adds independent support for the No case. The rest is judgment: how much weight to give the MTV signal against reports of an explicit understanding against referral. Two separate sources describe that understanding, and even an agenda placement often ends in deferral. On that basis I take about 0.12, near the lower runs, rather than higher. I retrieved no sources on this run; the reference class is my own construction.
